pillars.label: DESKTOP REASONING
pillars.name: Local LLM Server
pillars.role: High-performance local inference server with model lifecycle, routing and telemetry.
pillars.problem: Local applications should not need to couple their product logic to every inference backend, model format or runtime process.
pillars.description: Local LLM Server exposes an OpenAI-compatible API across local backends such as GGUF and MLX, while managing model lifecycle, resident runtimes, configuration and observability.
pillars.strategicContribution: It separates product experience from inference complexity, allowing multiple applications to reuse the same local reasoning layer.

pillars.label: PRIVATE SPEECH
pillars.name: Local ASR Server
pillars.role: Privacy-first speech recognition server optimized for accuracy and latency.
pillars.problem: Meeting and voice data is highly sensitive, yet speech products often require sending recordings to remote infrastructure.
pillars.description: Local ASR Server records microphone and system audio, stores sessions locally and transcribes them with Whisper on Apple Silicon through a reusable API and interface.
pillars.strategicContribution: It creates a private speech-to-text foundation that can feed local reasoning workflows without making remote transcription the default.

pillars.label: ON-DEVICE MOBILE AI
pillars.name: Android Local LLM Harness
pillars.role: On-device LLM runtime harness for Android apps with tight resource control.
pillars.problem: Running an LLM on Android requires more than native bindings: applications need model integrity, lifecycle, memory handling, cancellation, telemetry and device evidence.
pillars.description: The harness builds these concerns around llama.cpp, with a shared architecture for native and Capacitor applications and a path from embedded inference to a future shared Android service.
pillars.strategicContribution: It extends the privacy-first stack from desktop to mobile and aims to reduce the repeated engineering required to add local models to Android products.

about.heading: I work where AI infrastructure, product strategy and communication meet.
bio: I am Daniele Moltisanti, a data and AI professional based in Milan. My work combines technical architecture, product thinking and the ability to turn complex AI systems into understandable decisions and usable experiences.
Alongside my professional work, I build local-first infrastructure and privacy-first products in public. I also write about AI architecture and strategy through stAI tuned and LinkedIn.
I am particularly interested in the last mile between a working model and a reliable product: integration, observability, evaluation, packaging, user experience and strategic adoption.
